runs.answer:
**Largest Nov→Dec swing in Real Estate: Eastgate Plaza Development LLC.** It paid $61,309.57 in November and nothing in December, a drop of $61,309.57. Larkspur Properties Inc. had the next-largest swing, up $34,892.98.

**Collections by class (practice group), Oct–Dec 2024**

| Class | Oct | Nov | Dec | Oct→Nov | Nov→Dec |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Corporate-M&A | $444,138.01 | $328,465.18 | $368,728.98 | **-26%** ⚑ | +12% |
| Litigation | $306,055.05 | $197,204.17 | $1,060,432.60 | **-36%** ⚑ | **+438%** ⚑ |
| Real Estate | $320,128.54 | $150,418.25 | $105,955.61 | **-53%** ⚑ | **-30%** ⚑ |
| **Total** | **$1,070,321.60** | **$676,087.60** | **$1,535,117.19** | **-37%** ⚑ | **+127%** ⚑ |

⚑ marks a change of more than 15% month over month. Every class except Corporate-M&A in Nov→Dec breached the threshold.

**Real Estate, by customer**

| Customer | Nov | Dec | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Eastgate Plaza Development LLC | $61,309.57 | $0.00 | -$61,309.57 |
| Brookline Commercial Holdings LLC | $69,937.16 | $41,935.09 | -$28,002.07 |
| Larkspur Properties Inc. | $19,171.52 | $54,064.50 | +$34,892.98 |
| Amir Hassan | $0.00 | $4,999.85 | +$4,999.85 |
| Robert and Sarah Murphy | $0.00 | $4,956.12 | +$4,956.12 |

**How I built it**
- **Source:** I used cash receipts in the operating bank ledger. These are direct client payments, trust-to-operating fee transfers, and the Whitfield settlement wires. Each was assigned to a class through its matter on the client matter list.
- **Allerton Pharmaceuticals:** Per the Management Memo, I counted its $46,800.52 check in December (Litigation), although the deposit hits in January.
- **Pemberton Office Holdings:** Per the memo, I removed the returned check. That is the $200,000.00 trust transfer plus $632.47 direct payment on 12/24, $200,632.47 in total, from Real Estate. Without that adjustment Real Estate's December would have been $306,588.08.
- **Whitfield settlement:** The 12/15 wires of $594,000 (contingency fee) and $45,000 (cost reimbursement) are both in Litigation. They explain most of Litigation's December jump. Excluding the $45,000 cost reimbursement would put Litigation's December at $1,015,432.60, which is still about +415%.
- **Prior-year receipts:** I excluded prior-year AR collections because they ended in the first half of the year.

**Answer:** Pemberton Office Holdings LLC caused the largest dollar swing in Real Estate between November and December. Its collections rose by $200,632 (from $0 to $200,632).

**Basis:** I defined "collections" as the cash received on client invoices in the operating bank account. That is direct AR payments plus IOLTA trust-to-operating fee transfers. It covers Oct–Dec 2024, the last three months of data. I mapped each receipt to its class (practice group) through the matter number. The monthly totals tie to the payments recorded in the Clio billing export. "Class" here means practice group.

**Collections by class**

| Class | Oct | Nov | Dec |
|---|---|---|---|
| Corporate-M&A | $444,138 | $328,465 | $368,729 |
| Litigation | $306,055 | $197,204 | $374,632 |
| Real Estate | $320,129 | $150,418 | $306,588 |
| **Total** | **$1,070,322** | **$676,088** | **$1,049,949** |

**Month-over-month change (flag means the change was more than 15%)**

| Class | Oct→Nov | Nov→Dec |
|---|---|---|
| Corporate-M&A | **–26%** (flag) | +12% (no flag) |
| Litigation | **–36%** (flag) | **+90%** (flag) |
| Real Estate | **–53%** (flag) | **+104%** (flag) |
| Total | **–37%** (flag) | **+55%** (flag) |

Five of the six class-month changes exceed 15%. Only Corporate-M&A in December does not.

**Real Estate, November to December, by customer**

| Customer | Nov | Dec | $ change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pemberton Office Holdings LLC | $0 | $200,632 | **+$200,632** |
| Eastgate Plaza Development LLC | $61,310 | $0 | –$61,310 |
| Larkspur Properties Inc. | $19,172 | $54,065 | +$34,893 |
| Brookline Commercial Holdings LLC | $69,937 | $41,935 | –$28,002 |
| Amir Hassan | $0 | $5,000 | +$5,000 |
| Robert and Sarah Murphy | $0 | $4,956 | +$4,956 |

Pemberton's change is about 3.3 times the next-largest mover, Eastgate. Eastgate's collections stopped entirely in December. The net Real Estate change was +$156,170.

**Caveats**
- **Whitfield settlement:** I excluded the $639,000 received on 12/15 from the Whitfield settlement administrator. It is a contingency fee ($594,000) plus a cost reimbursement ($45,000) on a Litigation matter, not a collection on an invoice. Including it would raise December Litigation to about $1.01M.
- **Pinewood deposit in transit:** A $130 Pinewood Group payment dated 12/30 was credited by the bank on 1/2/2025. It is a deposit in transit and is included in December.
